AUTHOR: Sriram
TITLE: Enhanced YOLOv10 Framework Featuring DPAM and DALSM for Real-Time Underwater Object Detection
REGION: Tropical Australia (DeepFish); UOT32 mixed global sources
SPECIES: fish and other underwater objects (UOT32 classes); DeepFish fish
DATA: UOT32 underwater object tracking dataset (32 videos, 24,241 frames; 20,853 train / 5,214 test) and DeepFish
V_EV: Sec. IV.C: metrics reported 'across different environments, including bright shallow water, turbid conditions, low light, and deep sea scenarios.'
D2: UOT32: 20,853 train / 5,214 test images; k-fold CV for hyperparameter tuning; DeepFish split not stated
D_EV: Sec. II: 'contains 20,853 training images and 5,214 test images'; split unit and grouping never stated.
R_EV: Sec. V: 'The model was developed on the UOT32 dataset'; DeepFish results reported without stating training data, no in-domain vs external comparison.
E_EV: Sec. IV: evaluated 'on metrics that include precision, recall, mAP at IoU of thresholds 0.50 and 0.50-0.95, and the F1 Score.'
ARCH: YOLOv10s + DPAM (dual partial attention) + DALSM (dynamic adaptive label assignment, sun-glint removal) + Marine-Fusion Loss
NOTE: INCL=Y only because DeepFish (monitoring dataset) results are reported (Table 3/Sec. IV.C, e.g. 'accuracy of 0.85 and mAP of 0.89' in bright shallow water); headline results are on UOT32 (a tracking benchmark of mixed sources incl. controlled settings).
